name: Gated Attention · elementwise
tagline: A sigmoid gate computed from the block input scales every channel of every head's SDPA output before the output projection.
description: The Dense Baseline's full causal attention with the paper's best gate (elementwise, head-specific, multiplicative, sigmoid): Y' = Y ⊙ σ(X W_θ), where Y is each head's SDPA output and X the block's pre-normalized input. W_θ is a bias-free 1536 × 1536 layer, output_gate, initialized with c_q's uniform rule and trained by AdamW in the auxiliary group, as the paper trained it; c_q, c_k, c_v and c_proj stay with Muon. The gate costs about 7% of the shared budget at 23 layers, so calibration reduced the depth to 21 layers and widened the FFN to 6272; the model has one value-embedding table fewer than Dense.
paperTitle: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free
mechanism: Y' = Y ⊙ σ(X W_θ) on each head's SDPA output, before c_proj; X is the block's pre-normalized input
W_θ: bias-free 1536 × 1536 output_gate, c_q's uniform initialization, AdamW (auxiliary group)
21 full-attention layers, FFN 6272, 11 value-embedding tables; RoPE, QK norm and the zero-initialized c_proj unchanged
limitations: Single seed 42. Under the shared compute budget the gate is paid for with two of Dense's 23 layers and one value-embedding table, so the comparison with Dense mixes the gate with that depth and capacity change; Gated Attention · headwise keeps Dense's shell exactly. The official code fuses W_θ into q_proj and trains every weight with AdamW; here W_θ is a separate layer so that it can stay with AdamW while c_q uses Muon. Parameters, memory and speed are outcomes, not controls.
